title: How dangerous are rollercoasters?
description:
A passenger recently died following an incident on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. And Six Flags Magic Mountain has permanently closed its X2 coaster after multiple rider injury reports. These separate events have led many roller coaster enthusiasts to ask how safe roller coasters actually are. BBC reporter William Lee Adams joins us to talk about what’s been going on at Six Flags, how common accidents and serious injuries are, and what safety checks are in place.

We also hear from Ryan the Ride Mechanic, a former amusement park mechanic and YouTuber who spent 14 years in the industry. He explains how safety is built into the design process, how amusement parks complete further checks during installation, and what daily checks take place to keep riders safe.

summaryEn: This episode of BBC's What in the World explores roller coaster safety following recent incidents at Six Flags theme parks in the US, including a fatal ejection on the Goliath coaster and brain injury reports linked to the X2 coaster. BBC reporter William Lee Adams and former amusement park mechanic Ryan discuss the extreme rarity of roller coaster injuries and fatalities compared to lightning strikes or car accidents. Ryan details the multi-layered safety protocols in place, from third-party design reviews and accelerometer testing to rigorous daily pre-opening inspections of tracks, restraints, and collision-prevention block systems.
